sources.title: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi on raising $10 billion, fighting for AI talent, and someday going public
sources.quote_checked: It's actually quite a logistical operation, raising $10 billion compared to previous rounds. | I probably underestimated the sheer number of investors and the amount of interest. | It's a war for AI talent right now, especially with OpenAI, Anthropic. | This is happening every day, and the talent market for AI is insane. | I think absolutely, theoretically, the earliest we'd go public would be sometime next year. | But this does give us flexibility to start providing liquidity opportunities for our employees.

sources.title: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi interview (Mad Money with Jim Cramer)
sources.venue: CNBC's Mad Money, transcript via CEOInterviews.AI
sources.quote_checked: AI doesn't have an intelligence problem. AI has a context problem. How do we feed it that context? | The Lakehouse has become the system of record nowadays. | Costs a lot of money to loop through all the data. | For Databricks, we don't burn any money at all, $0. So for us, we can choose the timing.

sources.title: Databricks CEO Ghodsi: Data Governance is AI's True Enterprise Bottleneck
sources.by: StartupHub.ai staff (reporting CNBC's Closing Bell Overtime, interviewer Jon Fortt)
sources.quote_checked: It's actually the governance of the data that's the problem. | It's not like we can't access that data, that data is there... | It's because of privacy.

sources.quote_checked: With this investment, we're deepening our commitment to help every organization innovate with AI on their own data | we're giving customers a unified foundation to build trusted, high-performance Data Intelligent Applications at scale.
